workflow: A comparison obtains a pointer into a mutable buffer and begins iterating over its contents.
Element decoding invokes user-controlled code that releases or resizes the underlying buffer during the comparison.
The comparison continues using the previously obtained pointer after its backing storage has been invalidated.
A later access reaches freed memory, causing a use-after-free failure instead of a recoverable mutation error.
summary: Reentrant buffer mutation invalidates an active comparison pointer
decision_reason: The bug materially matches the existing reentrant cleanup workflow: user-controlled reentry mutates or releases storage while an outer operation still holds and later uses its address, producing use-after-free.
